visualReview.notes: Inspected the current plaza approach and all four turntable directions, the west façade and its Roman-numeral clock, the open bell tiers, the south windows, the tower and sanctuary domes, the attached rear volumes, and the view into the open north court. Reframed the tower and corrected the side and rear arched doors in the first pass.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected the nine placement and shared-surface frames. Lime plaster, pale limestone detail, ceramic domes, timber doors and metal bells remain readable. The geographic viewer fixture unloaded cleanly.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all 25 medium-fi views and the explicit skyline, district, street and closeup comparisons. The single projecting tower, clock, three nave surfaces, five domes, compound silhouette and open court carry across levels. Main portal, arch surrounds, saints and bell details resolve in the near levels.

geographicReview.notes: OpenStreetMap way 310133177 identifies the cathedral and the west front on the plaza. Current independent Terrarium data establish the plaza datum and rear slope. The ground was inspected separately with no cutout. The geographic fixture serves as a flat placement check; individual thresholds and exact rear sections remain approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: Present-day cathedral exterior. Include the plaza frontage, north clock and bell tower, the nave and side aisles, and the attached sacristy and chapel. Preserve the open court where supported by the plan.
fidelityReview.notes: The original 1859 plate fixes the composition of the carved west façade, domed tower, south wall, arches and buttresses. Written restoration and municipal accounts give the clock stage, bell tier, five domes, three naves, north yard and chapel. Exact present colors, heights, yard paving, rear divisions and ornament profiles are estimates.

imageryReview.notes: Started with published Qualla originals. Omitted the unconfirmed anonymous photo and the postcard without an independently established edition as well as modern attribution-only images. The full original 1859 page with caption was inspected and bound to the University of Pennsylvania Libraries record confirming its original publication and rights declaration.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Standing Comayagua Cathedral exterior and attached ranges, anchored to Plaza León Alvarado, including the open north courtyard.

limitations: Public-domain 1859 engraving guides the plaza elevation and south wall. Present clock placement, five domes, relief motifs and the open north patio follow the documented standing cathedral.

The native mapped perimeter and original elevation field fix scale, orientation and grade. The division of the rear chapel and chapter ranges, the paving, the exact thresholds and individual section heights are estimates.

Model scope is the cathedral exterior. The carved saints and heraldic and botanical relief are simplified silhouettes at landmark scale; the historic atrium railing in the engraving is outside the standing exterior scope.
